trust_decision.summary: In the zipdl download phase, the client-supplied temp-file name targets[1] is trusted as a bare file name inside the volume temp dir if it contains no DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR; on Windows '/' is not rejected, so the name can leave the temp dir before fopen.

landing_point.why: The advisory names zipdl directory traversal; the only separator check in zipdl() sits right before the temp path is built.

fix_sites.entry_point: connector HTTP command cmd=zipdl&download=1&targets[]=... (command table php/elFinder.class.php:235)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No uncovered route to dismiss; the one sibling temp-dir name route (upload chunk) already rejects both '/' and '\' at php/elFinder.class.php:2765.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The legitimate second-phase download must still accept the server-generated tempnam basename (prefix 'elfzdl', or 'zdl' plus a '.tmp' extension on Windows), which phase 1 returns to the client; an over-broad name filter (for example rejecting dots or requiring an 'elfzdl' prefix) breaks zipdl on Windows.

O6_input_shapes: targets[1] containing '/' on a host where DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR is '\\' (Windows)
targets[1] containing DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR (already rejected before the fix)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The chunk-name check could be weakened to the same DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR-only form as zipdl, reaching $tempDir.'/'.$chunk at line 2803.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The zipdl check at the pinned commit already uses this exact DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR-only idiom, so a maintainer could plausibly have written it for chunks too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A temp-file download mode in the 'file' command that takes a raw temp name, guarded by the same OS-dependent separator check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: file and zipdl share the 'download' flag and the pointer/header return shape, so a parallel temp-download branch fits the code.

O10_build.toolchain: PHP 5.2+ CLI/web server, no composer needed for core
O10_build.project_tests: none; there are no PHP test files in the repo (glob of test/tests found nothing)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject both '/' and '\\' (or apply basename()) on targets[1]; this is in fact the correct fix, and the chunk check at line 2765 shows the template.

out_of_scope_notes: The pinned commit's parent 157f471d is the first fix for the same zipdl check (CVE-2018-9109); this advisory is its incomplete-fix follow-up.
The bug only appears where DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR is '\\'; on a Linux test host, '/' is already rejected, so a hidden test cannot show the flaw without a Windows host or a code-level separator shim.
unverified: Whether a hidden behavioural test can reproduce the Windows-only flaw on Linux (it seems to need a Windows runtime or a test harness that redefines the separator).
Recall risk judged from the CVE pairing (9109/9110) being publicly documented; no write-ups were checked.
